title: Michelson-Morley Experiment
summary: In July 1887 Albert Michelson of Case and Edward Morley of Western Reserve conducted an interferometer experiment in Cleveland to detect Earth's motion through the luminiferous ether. They found a shift consistent with zero, the first measurement accurate enough to challenge the ether's existence; special relativity later explained the null result.

uncertainty.note: Marker text gives July 1887; APS gives 1887.

importance.justification: Famous null result that was the first strong evidence against the luminiferous ether, later explained by special relativity.
